qe: If in a code language, DANCER is written as DGEPSF, then how PUBLIC will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में DANCER को DGEPSF लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में PUBLIC को क्या लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (2-Letter Pair Cross Pattern Method):
Step 1: 'DANCER' ko 2-2 letters ke pairs me baantein:
- Pair 1 (D A) with +3: A(1)+3 = 4 (D), D(4)+3 = 7 (G) → 'DG'
- Pair 2 (N C) with +2: C(3)+2 = 5 (E), N(14)+2 = 16 (P) → 'EP'
- Pair 3 (E R) with +1: R(18)+1 = 19 (S), E(5)+1 = 6 (F) → 'SF'
Logic: Har 2-letter pair ko cross karke kramashah +3, +2, +1 shift kiya gaya hai.
Step 2: 'PUBLIC' par same pairs aur shift lagayein:
- Pair 1 (P U) cross with +3:
  $$U(21) + 3 = 24 (X), \quad P(16) + 3 = 19 (S) \implies \text{'XS'}$$
- Pair 2 (B L) cross with +2:
  $$L(12) + 2 = 14 (N), \quad B(2) + 2 = 4 (D) \implies \text{'ND'}$$
- Pair 3 (I C) cross with +1:
  $$C(3) + 1 = 4 (D), \quad I(9) + 1 = 10 (J) \implies \text{'DJ'}$$
Combined Code: XS + ND + DJ = XSNDDJ.
Correct option (D) XSNDDJ hai.

Method 2 (First Pair Cross Shortcut):
U(21) + 3 = 24 (X), P(16) + 3 = 19 (S) → Shuruat 'XS' se hogi (Options A aur C eliminate). Middle pair L(12)+2 = 14 (N) aayega (Option B me 'M' hai, eliminate). Keval Option (D) bachta hai.
Sahi uttar (D) hai.

qe: If in a code language, VENTURE is written as CUZXQCQ, then how PAINTER will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में VENTURE को CUZXQCQ लिखा जाता है, तो उसी भाषा में PAINTER को क्या लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Segmented Cross Pattern Shortcut):
Step 1: 7-letter word ko (2 + 3 + 2) ke teen groups me baantein:
- Group 1 (First 2 letters - V E): Cross shift with -2, -1:
  $$E(5) - 2 = 3 (C), \quad V(22) - 1 = 21 (U) \implies \text{'CU'}$$
- Group 2 (Middle 3 letters - N T U): Reverse cross with +5, +4, +3:
  $$U(21) + 5 = 26 (Z), \quad T(20) + 4 = 24 (X), \quad N(14) + 3 = 17 (Q) \implies \text{'ZXQ'}$$
- Group 3 (Last 2 letters - R E): Cross shift with -2, -1:
  $$E(5) - 2 = 3 (C), \quad R(18) - 1 = 17 (Q) \implies \text{'CQ'}$$
Combined Code: CUZXQCQ.
Step 2: 'PAINTER' par same pattern lagayein:
- Pehle 2 (P A): $A(27) - 2 = 25 (Y), \; P(16) - 1 = 15 (O) \implies \text{'YO'}$
- Middle 3 (I N T): $T(20) + 5 = 25 (Y), \; N(14) + 4 = 18 (R), \; I(9) + 3 = 12 (L) \implies \text{'YRL'}$
- Aakhiri 2 (E R): $R(18) - 2 = 16 (P), \; E(5) - 1 = 4 (D) \implies \text{'PD'}$
Final Code: YOYRLPD.
Correct option (A) YOYRLPD hai.

Method 2 (Option Elimination by First & 3rd Letter):
- Pehla letter $A(27) - 2 = 25 (Y)$ aayega, isliye 'Z' se shuru hone wale Options (B) aur (D) eliminate ho gaye.
- Teesra letter $T(20) + 5 = 25 (Y)$ hoga, Option (C) me teesra letter 'Z' diya hai. Keval Option (A) bachta hai.
Sahi uttar (A) hai.

qe: If in a code language, RAIL is written as KCTN, then how READ will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में RAIL को KCTN लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में READ को क्या लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (3-Letter Cross + Direct Last Letter Method):
Step 1: 'RAIL' ka cross structure dekhein:
- Pehle 3 letters (R A I) ko reverse cross karke sabhi me +2 kiya gaya hai:
  $$I(9) + 2 = 11 (K)$$
  $$A(1) + 2 = 3 (C)$$
  $$R(18) + 2 = 20 (T)$$
- Chautha letter 'L' seedha +2 shift hota hai:
  $$L(12) + 2 = 14 (N)$$
Code ban gaya: K C T N.
Step 2: 'READ' par same logic apply karein:
- Pehle 3 letters (R E A) reverse cross with +2:
  $$A(1) + 2 = 3 (C)$$
  $$E(5) + 2 = 7 (G)$$
  $$R(18) + 2 = 20 (T)$$
- Aakhiri letter 'D' direct +2:
  $$D(4) + 2 = 6 (F)$$
Code: CGTF.
Correct option (B) CGTF hai.

Method 2 (First Letter Elimination Trick):
Pehla letter word ke 3rd letter se banega: $A(1) + 2 = 3 (C)$. Options (A) aur (C) 'B' se shuru ho rahe hain, isliye eliminate ho gaye. Last letter $D(4) + 2 = 6 (F)$ aayega, jisse Option (D) eliminate ho gaya.
Sahi uttar (B) hai.

qe: If in a code language, UPDATE is written as FRWCRY, then how BLENDY will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में UPDATE को FRWCRY लिखा जाता है, तो उसी भाषा में BLENDY को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Two Halves Reverse Cross (+2 / -2) Method):
Step 1: 6-letter word ko do barabar hisson (3-3 letters) me baantein:
- Pehla half (U P D) reverse cross with +2:
  $$D(4) + 2 = 6 (F)$$
  $$P(16) + 2 = 18 (R)$$
  $$U(21) + 2 = 23 (W) \implies \text{'FRW'}$$
- Doosra half (A T E) reverse cross with -2:
  $$E(5) - 2 = 3 (C)$$
  $$T(20) - 2 = 18 (R)$$
  $$A(27) - 2 = 25 (Y) \implies \text{'CRY'}$$
Combined: FRWCRY.
Step 2: 'BLENDY' par apply karein:
- First half (B L E) cross with +2:
  $$E(5) + 2 = 7 (G)$$
  $$L(12) + 2 = 14 (N)$$
  $$B(2) + 2 = 4 (D) \implies \text{'GND'}$$
- Second half (N D Y) cross with -2:
  $$Y(25) - 2 = 23 (W)$$
  $$D(4) - 2 = 2 (B)$$
  $$N(14) - 2 = 12 (L) \implies \text{'WBL'}$$
Code: GNDWBL.
Correct option (C) GNDWBL hai.

Method 2 (Fast Option Elimination):
- Pehla letter: $E(5) + 2 = 7 (G)$, isliye Options (B) aur (D) seedhe eliminate ho gaye.
- 5th letter: $D(4) - 2 = 2 (B)$ hona chahiye, Option (A) me 'C' diya hai, isliye (A) eliminate ho gaya.
Sahi uttar (C) hai.

qe: In a certain code language, EMPTY is written as NFOZU, then how KITES will be written in the same language?
qh: एक निश्चित कूट भाषा में EMPTY को NFOZU लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में KITES को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (2-Letter Pair Cross & Center Shift Method):
Step 1: 'EMPTY' ka structure analyze karein:
- Pehle do letters (E M) cross with +1: $M(13)+1 = 14 (N), \; E(5)+1 = 6 (F) \implies \text{'NF'}$
- Middle letter P: $P(16) - 1 = 15 (O)$
- Aakhiri do letters (T Y) cross with +1: $Y(25)+1 = 26 (Z), \; T(20)+1 = 21 (U) \implies \text{'ZU'}$
Combined Code: NFOZU.
Step 2: 'KITES' par same logic lagayein:
- Pehle do letters (K I) cross with +1:
  $$I(9) + 1 = 10 (J), \quad K(11) + 1 = 12 (L) \implies \text{'JL'}$$
- Middle letter T: $T(20) - 1 = 19 (S)$
- Aakhiri do letters (E S) cross with +1:
  $$S(19) + 1 = 20 (T), \quad E(5) + 1 = 6 (F) \implies \text{'TF'}$$
Code: JLSTF.
Correct option (A) JLSTF hai.

Method 2 (Direct Inspection Shortcut):
- Middle letter hamesha -1 ho raha hai: $T(20) - 1 = 19 (S)$.
- Options (B), (C), (D) me middle letter 'S' nahi hai, keval Option (A) me middle letter 'S' hai.
Sahi uttar (A) hai.
